title: Implement startup comparison
lead: Use the native SDK APIs while keeping browser observations, provider milestones and tuning conditions distinct.

items.label: Screen and controls: run a comparison

blocks.text: Each trial uses a fresh document and video element. Observers are registered before loading or requesting play. The comparison does not add a full hls.js or Shaka configuration editor; the adapters expose the public settings needed for this startup experiment.

rows: Player Web X

Use the playerx-hls bundle and Player(config), then sources.add and sources.attachVideo. Stage the source without data loading so its observers exist first. Start data loading with loadControl=2 and request source.play without waiting for Ready. Dispose the player when the trial ends.
hls.js

Use the full ESM build so alternate audio is available. Construct Hls, attachMedia(video), loadSource(url), then request video.play immediately for the fresh clear MediaSource attachment. Destroy the instance on cleanup.
Shaka Player

Use the official HLS-only ES2021 build, install polyfills and construct Player without a video argument. Require configure to return true, await attach(video), then start load(url, 0, "application/x-mpegurl") and video.play concurrently. Observe both promises and await destroy on cleanup.

blocks.text: A rejected or partly accepted configuration is not a default trial. Shaka can apply valid fields even when configure returns false, so the app rejects and destroys that candidate. Abort and cleanup also remove app-owned SDK listeners, video listeners and frame callbacks.

rows: Player Web X ready / playing
Preserve the real Source events. The native API has no load-completion promise.
hls.js hlsManifestParsed
Manifest parsing is observed as SDK readiness. It is not native playing, and is not a load-completion promise.
Shaka loaded
Preserve the loaded event and the separate load promise. started is a progress event and can occur without actual playback; it is not used as SDK Playing.

blocks.text: Use one clock and explicit intervals

Selection, SDK import, adapter milestones and native callbacks use the same parent performance clock. Times are relative to accepted content selection. Preloaded SDK import offsets may be negative; an on-demand import must not be corrected to zero to hide a clock error. Phases can overlap, so their durations are not added as an end-to-end total.

Playback startup (Play → Playing) is measured from the actual app play request to the native video playing callback. It is the explicitly defined VST-like interval in this app. Selection → Playing additionally includes work after content selection, such as SDK import and player construction. Play → moving frame separately records when a subsequent callback reports advancing media time.

First-frame time is recorded on entry to requestVideoFrameCallback using that same clock. The API reports frames submitted for composition, but this measurement is callback-observation time, not metadata.presentationTime or physical display time. A callback can arrive late under load. Browsers can also reduce clock precision; a real zero remains zero.

A paused frame can be observed before the play request. Its selection → frame value is still recorded; play → frame becomes missing with end-before-start rather than a fabricated zero. Successful playback additionally requires native playing, real media advancement and moving frames when the API is available. loadeddata is kept separate and never fills a missing frame observation.
Choose settings without claiming an optimum

Use the same fixed-rendition HLS source, en-labelled audio, start position zero, normal rate and muted playback. Optional Analytics collection, advertising and SDK UI are not added to the cohort. HTTP caching remains browser-managed in the public UI; preloaded describes SDK residency, not a warm network cache.

rows: Startup loading and retention

hls.js coordinates maxBufferLength, maxMaxBufferLength, backBufferLength and frontBufferFlushThreshold. Shaka uses streaming.bufferingGoal and bufferBehind. The startup retention candidate is 12 seconds forward and 6 seconds behind. These are duration goals, not total-memory limits.
Bounded tuning
hls.js enableWorker is evaluated as true/false; Shaka streaming.segmentPrefetchLimit as 0/1/2. A matching-version worker asset is bundled for hls.js. Shaka keeps its default rebufferingGoal of 0.
Player Web X data loading

Use loadControl=2 (Data) for this fresh-source playback comparison. Nothing (0) and Metadata (1) are valid APIs requesting no data or manifests only, but are excluded from this playback cohort. The standard HLS bundle does not expose the same buffer knobs as the other SDKs.
Other features and compatibility

DASH, DRM, offline playback, casting, advertising and live-only controls do not belong to this clear HLS startup case. Deprecated settings and v8 compatibility types are not treated as supported native Web X tuning APIs.

blocks.text: The configuration interfaces were reviewed by purpose: common conditions, startup candidates, other features, deprecated or compatibility settings, and custom hooks outside this experiment. This is a scope assessment, not full configuration API coverage. Screening uses a fixed Selection → Playing metric; new confirmation trials use the selected settings. A faster candidate for this short stream does not establish smooth or memory-efficient playback on every device and network.

rows: Adaptive quality and initial bandwidth
The selected master contains one video rendition. Keep hls.js abr/startLevel/testBandwidth and Shaka abr settings at their defaults; this experiment does not evaluate adaptive quality selection.
Manifest and codec checks
Pass the known HLS MIME type to Shaka load. Keep codec guessing and decoding-capability checks at their defaults; do not bypass compatibility checks to reduce a timing value.
Prefetch, transport and transmuxing

Keep hls.js startFragPrefetch=false and its experimental progressive=false at their defaults. They control loading before attachment completes and processing data during a download; automatic screening does not vary these paths. Use the existing loaders and avoid forcing Shaka to transmux the fMP4 input solely to use a worker.
Retries and recovery
Keep each SDK's normal request retries and MediaSource playback recovery. Every trial has the same outer 30-second deadline; expiry remains a failed attempt rather than a successful low startup time.
Logging

The Web X default profile retains its SDK log level; the startup profile explicitly selects Off. hls.js keeps debug=false and Shaka keeps its release logging configuration. SDK error events remain observed in both profiles.

blocks.text: Reviewing a setting is different from testing every value. Automatic screening varies the hls.js worker and Shaka prefetch limit only. The forward/back buffer durations are fixed candidates, and equal duration targets do not establish equal buffer implementations or memory use. Read the default and startup profiles as separate experiments.

items: Shaka getStats().loadLatency and timeToFirstFrame stay in seconds with the SDK’s own definitions. loadLatency ends at loadedmetadata; timeToFirstFrame uses its frame callback or loadeddata fallback. They have a different origin and observation method from the common metrics.

The native Web X bundle has no public getters for the active media backend, selected audio language, worker activity or the provider latency/bandwidth samples used here. Those fields remain null or unknown with a reason. Missing values do not establish poor performance.

hls.js observes the attached MediaSource instance. Shaka checks the actual MediaSource load mode, but may expose only the MediaSource family rather than its managed/regular subtype. A requested enableWorker value does not prove that a worker ran.

JavaScript heap delta covers only the exposed JavaScript heap, not decoder, GPU, worker or total process memory. Main-thread long tasks are not total CPU utilization. Resource Timing bytes cover observed entries; zero transfer size can have more than one cause and is not proof that no data was fetched.

blocks.text: What does a successful startup prove?

The trial must satisfy the adapter’s start contract and native playback checks, then finish cleanup. It is a short startup check, not an uninterrupted viewing or rebuffering test. Repeat longer playback checks separately before adopting a setting for production.

No. This app defines Playback startup as Play request → native playing, while Bitmovin Analytics defines VIDEO_STARTUPTIME using Play → TimeChanged; STARTUPTIME also includes PLAYER_STARTUPTIME. Collectors can have SDK-specific behavior. This cohort does not enable a collector or synthesize Dashboard values from browser events. Use the Analytics implementation guide for collection and Dashboard queries.
